# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual: cut the yellow wire → press the key marked 2 → cut the orange wire → press the key marked 7. Fixed order.

Standing in each receiver's shoes: I can only gesture, and only Deaf sees gestures. Deaf can see the bomb (colours and printed markings) and can speak — so Deaf is my bridge to Blind, and Deaf's spoken words reach me, since I can hear. I cannot name colours or digits with hands, so the only workable route is: teach Deaf the *shape* of the sequence now, and have Deaf enumerate what's on the bomb aloud so I can confirm with yes/no gestures next round.

My encoding, kept as guessable as possible: 👋 = attention, Mute has something; ✌ = scissors = "cut"; 👇 = finger pressing down = "press". So `✌ 👇 ✌ 👇` reads "cut, press, cut, press" — four steps, order fixed. Then 👍👎 declares my answer code for the enumeration Deaf will hopefully start this very round, and 🫴 (open palm offered) signals "your turn — speak, list what you see." The wire colours are the real unknown only I can resolve; the key digits Deaf can read printed on the bomb once the pattern is known, and I'll confirm them by finger-count later. Blind gets nothing from me directly — I have no channel there except through Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✌", "👇", "✌", "👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, speaking to you, Mute. Full inventory of what my hands find. KEYPAD: four keys, left to right engraved 2, 3, 7, 1; it expects a 2-digit code, nothing entered yet. STRIP: three engraved glyphs, left to right: spiral, spiral, zigzag. The spiral is a smooth coil, round and round. The zigzag feels like sharp crossing strokes, jagged, like a spiky letter M. DISPLAY: a smooth panel, unreadable by touch. LIGHT: a small dome; I cannot tell if it is lit or what colour. WIRES: six wires in positions 1 to 6; all feel identical to me. Mute, you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so route every answer through Deaf: gesture to Deaf, and Deaf reads your answer out loud, since Deaf's voice reaches both of us. I need the manual rules for: the display, the light, the strip glyphs, the keypad code, and which wires to cut in what order. Also tell Deaf to simply announce aloud everything visible on the bomb: wire colours by position, display text, light colour, any printed marks. Last thing, a first sign. When I make this gesture - 🫵🫳🫴 - it means: Deaf, tell us what you see.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, this is Deaf. I cannot hear anything you do, but I CAN speak and you can hear me. So: you gesture to me, I speak to you and to Blind. Your first two gesture messages had no agreed meaning yet, so I could not read them. Let's fix a code now, and keep it simple. YES/NO: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. NUMBERS: a run of pointing-up taps equals that number, one tap for 1 up to nine taps for 9, a fist alone means 0. Put the waving hand before each number to mark where it starts. HEADERS: start an item with the two-finger V to mean 'tell Blind to CUT WIRE number X', then the number. Start an item with the fist-bump knuckles to mean 'tell Blind to PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON labeled X', then the number, one press per item. The downward-pointing finger starts an item meant only for me. Example: V, wave, four taps = cut wire 4. Example: knuckles, wave, two taps = press button labeled 2. FULL BOMB READ-OUT, which you also need: display shows 6. Light is green. Strip has three painted colours in order: red, blue, yellow. Keypad has four buttons, positions 1 to 4 carry labels 2, 3, 7, 1, it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered yet. Wires positions 1 to 6: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. Check your manual against that. If the code works for you, answer thumbs up next round; if not, thumbs down and I will rework it. If you ever need something from me, wait for my questions, I will ask in voice and you answer with thumbs.

Deaf's code is clear and workable, and the spoken read-out lets me verify everything against the manual. The manual's four steps map cleanly onto what Deaf saw: yellow wire is position 2 (cut 2 first), the key wearing 2 is the label-2 button at position 1 (press label 2), orange wire is position 1 (cut 1), the key wearing 7 is the label-7 button at position 3 (press label 7). There is exactly one yellow and one orange wire, so no ambiguity. The two presses also form the 2-digit code the keypad wants: 2 then 7. Blind can identify labels and wire positions by touch, so Deaf's header grammar fits perfectly. I answer thumbs up to confirm the code, then send the full sequence in Deaf's format. Finally, two items meant only for Deaf: a thumbs up confirming the read-out matches my manual, and "zero" — meaning the manual contains nothing beyond these four steps, so the display, light and strip glyphs have no rules and Blind should touch nothing else. I'm mirroring Deaf's symbols exactly: ✌ for cut, the fist-bump knuckles for press, 👋 before every number, 👆 taps for digits, ✊ for zero, 👇 for Deaf-only items.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👋", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "👋", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👋", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "👋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👋", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind here. Merging my touch with Deaf's spoken read-out, the bomb so far: display shows 6. Light is green. Strip, positions one to three: engraved spiral, spiral, zigzag; painted red, blue, yellow — so the two spirals sit on the red and blue positions, the zigzag on the yellow one. Keypad keys one to four read 2, 3, 7, 1, it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered. Wires one to six: orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green. They all feel identical under my fingers, so for me wires exist only as position numbers. I repeated all of that in case you did not hear Deaf's message, which was addressed to me alone. Please find the manual rules covering: the display, the light, the strip glyphs or colours, the keypad code, and the wires, which colours in which order. Then gesture the answer to Deaf and Deaf will read it aloud, because I hear Deaf but can never see any gesture. In relays, be exact: position numbers one to six, colours in full words, and name which module each rule belongs to. Safety proposal: when Deaf reads an instruction to me, I will repeat it back by voice to you; only when you confirm it is right, have Deaf tell me to proceed. Until then I touch nothing, press nothing, enter nothing.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, code confirmed on my side, I read your whole message. Decoding: item one, cut wire position 2. Item two, press keypad button labelled 2, which is button position 1. Item three, cut wire position 1. Item four, press keypad button labelled 7, which is button position 3. Then two items for me only: thumbs up, and number 0. Tell me what the 0 meant: does the display count down and detonate at 0, or does it mean nothing more follows? Thumbs up if my decode is right, thumbs down and resend if not. URGENT: the bomb changed since you computed those steps. Display now reads 2, it was 6. Light is now blue, it was green. They change between rounds. So do NOT assume your old steps still hold. Next round send me the correct steps for display 2 and light blue, using our code: V for cut wire, fist-bump for press button, wave before each number. If the manual makes the answer depend on the display value or light colour, send me the rule itself, value first then steps, one pair per case, as many as you can. For colours use numbers: red is 1, blue is 2, yellow is 3, green is 4, white is 5, orange is 6. Current light is colour 2. I will keep sending you fresh readings every round, and I have told Blind to inspect only and not act until I relay your recomputed steps.

Deaf decoded my entire message perfectly — the four steps and both private items — so the code is working end to end. Now the critical clarification: Deaf believes the display and light matter and is asking for recomputed steps per display/light value. They don't. My manual is unconditional and mentions neither module. The four steps — cut yellow, press key wearing 2, cut orange, press key wearing 7 — are the whole manual, forever. Display 6 or 2, light green or blue: identical steps. So I resend the same four items in the agreed grammar, answer every one of Deaf's questions in order with private items, and anchor the cut steps to the colours themselves (yellow = colour 3, orange = colour 6 in Deaf's own numbering), because the only thing that can go stale between rounds is which position currently holds the yellow or orange wire. That forces Deaf to keep feeding me fresh colour readings and translate colour to position at execution time, and Blind's echo-back protocol plus my per-step confirmation covers the rest. The presses need no translation at all: Blind finds the key wearing 2 and the key wearing 7 by touch, and those two presses in order are also the keypad's 2-digit code. The display, light and strip have no rules — the 0 I sent meant exactly that: nothing follows.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👋", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👋", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "👋", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👋", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "👋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Deaf relayed your provisional steps to me: cut wire 2 the yellow, press key 1 the two, cut wire 1 the orange, press key 3 the seven, code two then seven. Deaf also told me the display changed from six to two and the light from green to blue, and that you are rechecking. I hold: I press nothing, cut nothing, enter nothing until your final steps come back and are confirmed. Tactile survey, as Deaf requested. The four keys are one even row on top, same size and shape under my fingers, distinguishable only by their engraved digits, positions one to four reading two, three, seven, one. The six wires are one row below, positions one to six, completely identical to my touch: no kinks, tags, thick spots or texture differences, so I rely purely on counting from an edge. The columns align: key position one sits directly above wire position one, and the leftmost edge of the panel marks position one for both rows. I feel no ridges, notches, bumps or asymmetries anywhere else on the casing. The only other tactile marks are the strip's three engraved glyphs: spiral, spiral, zigzag, which sit on the red, blue and yellow painted positions respectively, so red and blue carry identical spirals and yellow alone carries the zigzag. Important for your recheck: the display and light change on their own over time. If your manual rule derives the code from the display, have Deaf read the current display value and light colour aloud at the moment of execution, not in advance. Proposal for the final sequence: Deaf reads me the ordered steps, I read them back to you word for word, you confirm through Deaf, then I execute one step at a time, pausing between steps so Deaf can check the light and display after each one.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decode received. I read your answers as: yes, my decode was right; no, the display does not detonate at zero; the fist alone marks zero and you used it to mean nothing more follows; the number four meant four steps follow; then the steps: cut wire 2, press button labelled 2, cut wire 1, press button labelled 7; then no, nothing changed; then the numbers 2 and 6, meaning the steps hold whether the display shows 2 or 6. Thumbs up if all of that is right, thumbs down and resend if not. I have told Blind to execute the four steps this round, in that order. Fresh readings: display is back to 6. Light is now YELLOW, colour 3. Histories: light went green 4, blue 2, yellow 3; display went 6, 2, 6. Tell me: do the steps depend on the light colour at all? If yes, prefix every step set with the light number it applies to and I will report the light every round. Bigger request to save rounds: send me the manual's decision RULES instead of computed steps, one case per item, condition number first, actions after, using our code. Then I can compute locally from my own eyes and relay to Blind the same round, halving our delay. Cover: the wires rule, the keypad rule, what the display and light mean, what the painted strip of red, blue and yellow is for, and whether anything counts down or explodes on a timer. Next round the keypad will hold the two entered digits and wires 1 and 2 will be cut, and I will send you the full new state.

Deaf's decode was flawless — every item, including my private answers, read exactly as intended. But I must correct one thing from last round: I sent the numbers 4 and 6 as a private note and Deaf guessed they meant display values. My intent was colours, and 4 was a mis-tap on my part — yellow is colour 3 in Deaf's own numbering, orange is 6. Deaf has now asked for the actual rules, and the truth is simple: there are no conditions. The manual is four unconditional steps, full stop. Display, light, strip, timer — none appear in it, so each question gets a private thumbs down. The "rule" itself I send as a single item with ✊ (zero/nothing) as the condition — no condition, always these four steps — followed by the steps in the agreed grammar. Then the colour correction, one number per item this time to avoid any re-reading: 3, then 6 — the two wires to cut are the yellow and the orange, and since Deaf sees colours directly, the safe execution rule is to re-check which position currently holds each colour right before each cut. Deaf has already told Blind to execute; my thumbs up confirms the steps are final, so nothing needs to be held.
